From:Salesforce Support <sfsupport@probomedical.com>Sent:Friday, August 14, 2026 7:35 PMCc:David Okolo <dokolo@probomedical.com>; Christine Meier <cmeier@probomedical.com>; Ginny McGrath <GMcGrath@probomedical.com>Subject:Salesforce Update: LOGIN CHANGE: Phishing-Resistant Multi-Factor Authentication

table:table-cell.text:p: You have been included on this email because you have special access within Salesforce that is being affected by an upgrade coming from Salesforce. Starting August 16th, you will see a screen when logging into Salesforce that indicates you must create a passkey (see screenshot below). You will be required to set a new passkey to continue to use Salesforce.

What is changing?: Salesforce is enforcing phishing-resistant Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) for all users with a System Administrator profile or special super user access. Thisis differentfrom the current MFA verification we have been using in the past: Microsoft Authenticator or Salesforce Authenticator. The special MFA requires methods known as Passkeys which are built-in authenticators or physical security keys. The good news is we can use built-in authenticators such as Touch ID, Windows Hello, or your mobile phone.
When is the change occurring? Our production instance is scheduled to go live August 16th. Your first login after that will require you to set it up. All logins after that will require you to use it.

What do I need to do? Click on the create passkey and it will give you the options of what to set up. If you use your phone/tablet you will likely use Face ID as your method. If using your computer, you can use the Windows Hello authenticator where it will set up a passkey leveraging your computer password. If you are in your browser, it may default to setting it up there (i.e., Google Password Manager if you are in Chrome.) If you would prefer one of the other options, you can choose “Choose Another Verification Method.”
